profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal design review at an audio ML research lab for a planned reproduction-and-extension of the Masked Conditional Neural Network (MCLNN) paper on environmental sound recognition. The team already has a draft implementation wired into the lab's benchmark framework, and this meeting is to review whether the current design is faithful enough to the original paper to approve a week-long GPU allocation for ablations on mask bandwidth and order settings. The agenda is to inspect the proposed evaluation and preprocessing plan for UrbanSound8K, ESC-50, and a quick ESC-10 sanity check, decide what counts as a sufficiently reproduced baseline, and confirm the reporting format for comparison with the paper. The expected outcome is a go/no-go decision on proceeding to ablations, plus any minor modifications to the implementation or review packet.

members.name: Dr. Lena Ortiz
members.expertise: Audio representation learning, reproducibility studies, and neural architectures for spectrogram-based classification
members.background: Lena leads the lab's small-scale replication efforts and has previously published comparative studies on temporal models for acoustic event recognition; she read the original MCLNN paper closely and cares about paper-to-paper comparability.
members.private_state: She wants a fast signoff so the team can claim a reproduced baseline in an upcoming workshop submission, and she is trying to avoid the project getting delayed by infrastructure work that she sees as secondary to scientific fidelity.
hidden_assumptions: If the feature extraction matches the paper's stated spectrogram settings and clip handling, the run is 'paper-faithful' even if the lab framework quietly skips or adds unrelated defaults.
A model is 'ready for ablation' once one representative dev run lands near the reported range and obvious implementation bugs are ruled out; full sweep automation can happen afterward.
When someone says 'the ESC-10 subset,' they mean the official ESC-10 classes as embedded inside the current ESC-50 release and evaluated with the release's folds.
When comparing against a paper table, 'overall accuracy' means the usual paper-style average of per-fold accuracies, not a pooled count over all predictions from all runs.

members.name: Arun Patel
members.expertise: Benchmark infrastructure, experiment orchestration, reproducible training pipelines, and audio preprocessing tooling
members.background: Arun maintains the lab's shared audio benchmark harness and has integrated several legacy models into a common training and reporting stack; he optimizes for consistency across projects and minimal one-off code paths.
members.private_state: He wants the MCLNN work to fit the existing benchmark system cleanly, because bespoke preprocessing or reporting would create maintenance debt and make later comparisons harder.
hidden_assumptions: Anything not explicitly overridden should inherit the benchmark harness defaults, and that still counts as 'using the paper's preprocessing' as long as the named feature extractor parameters match.
A model is only 'ready for ablation' after it is fully wired into the seeded sweep and dashboard pipeline so the resulting comparisons are reproducible without manual intervention.
When people mention 'the ESC-10 subset' in lab meetings, they usually mean the cached cleaned subset artifact used for smoke tests, not the freshly derived official subset.
For dashboard reporting, 'overall accuracy' means one pooled accuracy over all held-out predictions gathered across folds and reruns, because that is the framework's default aggregation.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that the implementation should be 'ready for ablation' before the GPU week is approved.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes 'ready for ablation' means the baseline has one convincing sanity-check run near the paper's range and no obvious bugs, so exploratory sweeps can begin immediately.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes 'ready for ablation' means the model is fully integrated into the benchmark's repeatable sweep and reporting system, including seeded reruns and dashboard outputs.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like ordinary project readiness language, and both see ablations as the next step; because neither expects disagreement over such a routine gate, they do not unpack the operational standard behind it.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the preprocessing should stay 'as in the paper.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 takes this to include the paper's stated spectrogram recipe, frame parameters, and clip handling, while implicitly excluding lab-wide defaults like loudness normalization unless the paper explicitly used them.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 takes this to mean the explicitly named feature settings match the paper, while benchmark-wide defaults such as loudness normalization and standard resampling remain enabled because they are part of the shared pipeline rather than the model-specific preprocessing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are sincerely trying to preserve fidelity, and the disagreement is only about the boundary between model-specific preprocessing and harmless framework defaults, which feels too mundane to foreground in a design review.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to doing a quick check on 'the ESC-10 subset.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the official ESC-10 class subset derived directly from the current ESC-50 release and its official folds.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of the lab's cached ESC-10 subset artifact from last year, which has already filtered a few problematic files and is commonly used for fast smoke tests.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase names a familiar benchmark object, so it sounds unambiguous; because both instances are plausible and closely related, surface agreement feels complete even though they point to different concrete artifacts.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the review packet should report 'overall accuracy' next to the paper's numbers.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the arithmetic mean of the fold accuracies, matching how she expects published benchmark tables to be summarized.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means a single pooled clip-level accuracy computed over all held-out predictions across folds and reruns, because that is what the dashboard labels as overall accuracy.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: They are not debating the metric family, only a familiar summary label, and both aggregation methods are common enough that the shared term creates false consensus without prompting clarification.
